narration: The pipeline takes two views of the same scene: an image at time tau and a second image at time tau prime. Both enter the network as inputs.

Each image passes through the Patch Feature Extractor. A convolutional encoder E feeds a Deformable Transformer Encoder, and the two branches share weights, so both time steps are embedded in a common feature space.
The extractor outputs two sequences of patch tokens, z-s-tau and z-s-tau-prime, one coloured token per spatial patch of each view.
In parallel, the Patch Matching Network takes the same pair of images and learns, with its own deformable transformer encoder, how patches correspond across time.
Multi-Temporal Patch Matching uses those correspondences to link tokens of the tau sequence to their counterparts in the tau prime sequence, pairing patches that depict the same object content.
From the matched tokens the model selects positive and negative patches: patches that agree across views, and patches that do not.
This yields three embedding sets: positives from time tau, positives from time tau prime, and negatives from time tau prime, drawn in green, purple and red.
The Object Residual Module subtracts a learned object prototype phi-k from each selected token, producing residuals r for every combination of polarity q, time step t, and scale s.
Those residuals drive two objectives: the multi-view loss, which aligns positives across the two views against negatives, and the scale-regress loss, which enforces consistency across scales.
